samples.question: The picture shows six solid coloured STRIPS, one red, one green, one blue, one orange, one purple and one brown. Every strip is a horizontal bar drawn in its own row, and no two strips share a row. Each strip SPANS the left-to-right stretch between its own two ends; how high or low its row sits, the order of the rows, and the colour of a strip all mean nothing. Imagine sliding one straight VERTICAL line across the whole picture from left to right and, at each place, counting how many strips that line passes through. The DEPTH of a place is that count. The answer is the LARGEST depth reached anywhere. The vertical line is never drawn, the deepest place is never marked, and no strip is special: the deepest place is where the most spans happen to lie one above another, which may be anywhere along the picture. A strip counts at a place only if the line passes strictly inside its span; touching an end never happens, because no two strip ends line up. The number of strips, six, is the same in every picture and is not the answer. The total coloured length, the longest strip, the shortest strip, the widest gap, the number of strips reaching the left or the right of the picture, and the place along the picture where the deepest stack sits are each the answer no more often than chance allows. Pale grey vertical rules and the grey line along the bottom are decoration and mean nothing. What is the largest depth reached anywhere? Answer 2, 3, 4 or 5.
